title: How much text a screen should hold
statement: How much text one screen should hold at each grade is unsettled: a sparse screen suited to early grades was judged right for older readers decoding archaic language.
example: In one build meeting a Grade 9 prototype screen was put at maybe a grade three or four kind of sparseness.
detail: In a build meeting on 7 October 2026, one participant asked whether there was a view on how much text should be on a screen, put a Grade 9 prototype's screen at maybe a grade three or four kind of sparseness and asked for a Grade 9 metric, while calling that a guess with no background in learning science (`g9/sources/meeting-notes/Incept Service CoE Catchup - 2026_10_07 10_30 CEST - Notes by Gemini.md`, lines 518-532). Another participant answered that learners were already decoding the text's archaic language, so the amount shown was accessible, and more could come where they are confident (lines 542-550). No density measure by grade is on record.

noting that the current sparse UI appeared more suited to Grade 3 or 4
observed that the limited text density works well for decoding complex Elizabethan language, but agreed to establish clear guidelines to eliminate guesswork and limit necessary design iterations
